newsitem.title: UK: Product tanker market saw limited activity this week.
newsitem.headline: Product tanker market saw limited activity this week.

text.p: Clean tanker markets saw only limited activity in most regions this week, but Mediterranean and Middle East markets remained buoyant on a combination of good demand and tight tonnage avails, Brokers said.

Brokers E.A. Gibson said in their weekly report that a shortage of tonnage had helped create a buoyant Middle east market which saw rates continuing to rise. They said end/Oct early Nov avails in the region were very thin forcing rates for 30,000 tonne cargoes up to around W240 with longer haul voyages for modern tonnage seeing increases to around W250 for voyage to S.Korea/Japan.

In the Mediterranean good trade was seen for owners of naphtha suitable tonnage. Cargoes of around 27,500 tonnes for cross Med voyage took around W210 and gas oil liftings from the Black Sea to the Med were fixed at W90.

E.A. Gibson said that as a result of this continuing tight market, a number of charterers were endeavouring to keep their enquiries at a low profile and this strategy had left the market looking artificially quiet.
European trade remained thin although rates were generally stable. Inter UK-Cont trade dull and transatlantic trade slow.
